label: neiso 19 ct mustrun
definition: neiso 19 (PROBE — rejected for the 2025 CC gap; informative on the CT wedge). Baseline (neiso 17) + --ct-mustrun-per-plant: forces each CT_PEAKER to its observed EIA-923 monthly net generation (the full reliability/reserve wedge, WEFOR/POF-exempt), vs baseline's sub-marginal --ct-deployment slice. CT_PEAKER TWh (model / EIA-923 %): 0.350 -15% / 0.356 -45% / 0.270 -46% (2023/24/25) vs baseline 0.084/0.052/0.079 (-80/-93/-84%) — recovers the wedge (2025 0.08->0.27; capped below 0.50 actual because the 2025 early-release 923 lists only 247 CT plants). Answers the candidate-B question: the reserve wedge (observed-energy floor) IS larger than the sub-marginal slice (cf. neiso 20 ct-deploy2x at 0.15 TWh). BUT CC_REGULAR barely moves: +8.7%->+8.4% in 2025 (-0.18 TWh, ~1:1 with the CT added) — the CT wedge is real but ~0.4 TWh, far too small to close the +4.6 TWh CC over-dispatch. ST_GAS (-95%) untouched (CT-only lever). 2023/24 CC stay in tol (-0.6/-0.7%). Verdict: correct physics, wrong magnitude for the headline gap; keep as the CT-class fix, not the CC fix.
